literal: The lack of natural character of being submissive towards one's wife, at all times, among noble people, shame will bring.
translation: The unmanly nature of bowing submissively to one's wife will always bring shame when one stands among worthy men.
modern: தன் மனைவியிடம் பணிந்துபோகும் ஆண்மையற்ற குணம், எப்போதும் நல்லவர்களிடையே அவமானத்தையே தரும்.
explanation: This couplet highlights the loss of social dignity that comes from being overly submissive to one's wife. The phrase 'இல்லாள்கண் தாழ்ந்த' refers to behaving subserviently to the mistress of the house, and 'இயல்பின்மை' (literally, 'lack of natural character') denotes a lack of the strength and independence expected of a householder. Such submissiveness, the poet warns, will 'எஞ்ஞான்றும்' (always) bring 'நாணு' (shame or embarrassment) when the man stands 'நல்லாருள்' (among noble or worthy people). It emphasizes that a man who loses his authority at home cannot command respect in the wider society.
